skill.name: skill-judge
skill.description: Evaluate Agent Skill design quality against official specifications and best practices. Use when reviewing, auditing, or improving SKILL.md files and skill packages. Provides multi-dimensional scoring and actionable improvement suggestions.
skill.summary: Review Agent Skill packages with a structured quality rubric and actionable SKILL.md improvement guidance.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Static analysis matched markdown code fences, inline code examples, and ordinary rubric text. I found no executable code, outbound network behavior, prompt-injection attempt, or reconnaissance intent in the cited files.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **First Pass - Knowledge Delta Scan**: Read the SKILL.md and categorize each section as:
- `description`: **THE MOST CRITICAL FIELD** — determines if skill gets used at all
[`docx-js.md`](docx-js.md) (~500 lines) completely from start to finish.
**Do NOT load** `ooxml.md` or `redlining.md` for this task.
When a Skill explains "what is PDF" or "how to write a for-loop", it's compressing knowledge Claude
| 4-7 | Generic warnings ("avoid errors", "be careful", "consider edge cases") |
| 11-13 | Valid frontmatter, description has WHAT but weak on WHEN |
| 0-5 | Severely mismatched (rigid scripts for creative tasks, vague for fragile ops) |
| Creative/Design | High freedom | Multiple valid approaches, differentiation is value | frontend-de
Symptom: Rigid scripts for creative tasks, vague guidance for fragile operations

content.value_statement: Many skill packages waste context with generic guidance and weak activation text. Skill Judge provides a scoring framework for SKILL.md reviews with evidence-based improvements.
actual_capabilities: Classifies skill content as expert, activation, or redundant knowledge.
Scores eight dimensions, including knowledge delta, anti-pattern quality, and specification compliance.
Checks frontmatter, description triggers, structure, and progressive disclosure guidance.
Identifies common failure patterns, such as tutorial content and orphan reference files.
Produces structured review reports with scores, issues, and top improvements.
limitations: It is a guidance-only skill and does not execute validation tools.
It focuses on skill design quality, not runtime security scanning.
It reflects examples and patterns described in its own files.
Large or unusual skill ecosystems may need additional human review.

use_cases.title: Review a Draft Skill
use_cases.description: Assess a SKILL.md before publishing and find the highest-impact improvements.

use_cases.title: Standardize Marketplace Review
use_cases.description: Apply the same quality rubric across submitted skill packages.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Skill Improvements
use_cases.description: Compare internal skills and decide which ones need refactoring first.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Skill Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this SKILL.md for quality. Identify the strongest issue, the likely grade, and the first three improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Rubric-Based Score
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill package with the Skill Judge rubric. Score each dimension and explain any score below 80 percent.

prompt_templates.title: Progressive Disclosure Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this multi-file skill for progressive disclosure. Check loading triggers, reference routing, and token waste.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Skill Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two skills with the Skill Judge framework. Rank them, explain trade-offs, and recommend a publish-ready version.

output_examples.input: A draft skill contains long basic tutorials and a short vague description.
output: The likely grade is low because the skill repeats knowledge the model already has.
The first fix is to rewrite the description with clear trigger scenarios.
The second fix is to replace basic tutorials with expert decision rules.

output_examples.input: A document skill has reference files but no instructions for when to load them.
output: The progressive disclosure score should be reduced.
Add explicit loading triggers at workflow decision points.
Add clear do-not-load guidance to prevent unnecessary context use.

output_examples.input: Two skills solve the same task, but one is shorter and more specific.
output: The shorter skill may rank higher if it preserves expert knowledge.
Compare knowledge delta, activation quality, and usability before choosing.

best_practices: Provide the complete SKILL.md and any referenced files for a fair review.
Ask for evidence by line or section when using results for publication decisions.
Treat scores as guidance and verify domain-specific claims with a human expert.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a malware scanner or dependency auditor.
Do not ask for high scores without providing the actual skill content.
Do not accept every suggested rewrite when it removes needed domain detail.

faq.question: What does Skill Judge evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates Agent Skill design quality, including knowledge delta, activation text, structure, and usability.

faq.question: Can it review skills for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The rubric applies to Agent Skill packages for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it run tests or execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a review framework and does not execute validation tools or project commands.

faq.question: What score makes a skill publishable?
faq.answer: The skill uses a 120-point rubric and letter grades. Final publishing decisions still need human judgment.

faq.question: Can it improve my SKILL.md?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies weak areas and suggests concrete improvements for descriptions, structure, and expert guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on design quality. Security review is still required before marketplace publication.
